audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Anivia/Anivia. The page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways.
audit.why: Neeko is at 58.54% here and the shape of the lane is not flat. Pre-6 Anivia is immobile and paying 80-100 mana a Flash Frost with an 11s cooldown at rank 1, and Neeko's E reaches 1000 against a 650-range Frostbite. Level 6 is the genuine coinflip — Glacial Storm plus the Rebirth egg. From her first item the lane is hers: Glacial Storm recycles in 4/3/2 and Crystallize is a flat 17s.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side = Neeko, phases[4].side stays Skill, phases[5..6].side = Anivia, whys rewritten to match, ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes said 'level 6 adds the ambush; Luden's makes the package lethal' — it hands Neeko both of the stages the chart does not give her.
audit.why: Level 6 is where Rebirth and Glacial Storm arrive, which is why the row is Skill and not Neeko: you can still all-in, but you have to kill her twice. The first-item stage belongs to Anivia — Tear and Lost Chapter turn her into a perma-shove with a wall.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is the kill pattern; level 6 the egg makes it a check; her first item takes the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all (defect 3), and the single most important interaction in the matchup was stated only as 'her E never doubles' with no explanation of what doubles it or from what range.
audit.why: Riot's Frostbite text is explicit: if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm, the damage doubles. That is the entire Anivia kill pattern, it is gated behind a slow 1075-range projectile, and Frostbite itself is a 4s cooldown at 650 range. None of those numbers were on the page.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Flash Frost 11s at 80 mana, Frostbite at 4s, Crystallize at a flat 17s and Glacial Storm at 4/3/2; report[5].t states the doubling condition properly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentioned that Neeko's E reaches 1000 against a 650-range Frostbite, which is the only reason the pre-6 all-in works.
audit.why: She has to walk 350 units into your root range to get her double-damage payoff, and she is immobile. That range gap is the matchup.
audit.corrected: phases[2].why now reads 'E outranges Frostbite by 350 — root at 1000, bloom the root, and she cannot answer at 650.'

audit.whatIsWrong: Anivia was addressed as he/his/him throughout the full layer — tldr, winCon, tradeGood, ahead, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, dosFull[0].t, dontsFull[2].t, report[0].t, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[4].t, report[9].t, report[11].t, report[13].t — while the content layer had her correctly as she/her.
audit.why: champ-gender lists anivia as female. The full layer came from a male-enemy template with the name swapped in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed on three bullets: dosFull[1].d (title 'Run clone mind-games on every reset') carried tradeGood; dontsFull[2].d (title about her key-spell window) carried tradeBad; dosFull[0].d (title 'Bloom her last-hit contact each cycle') carried the Flash Frost line. dontsFull[1].d also referenced 'assassin timers' against a champion with no dash and no stealth.
audit.why: Defect 2, plus a template phrase that is simply false about this enemy.
audit.corrected: All four bodies rewritten to answer their own titles from Anivia's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Placeholder phrasing: dontsFull[2].t and report[11].t both said 'his key-spell window' rather than naming the spell (defect 7). dosFull[2].t promised a 'triple-bloom' the kit does not describe.
audit.why: Riot's Q text says the seed blooms again on hitting champions — 'again', not three times. Naming the actual spell costs the same characters as the placeholder.
audit.corrected: 'Trade while Flash Frost is loaded' and 'Root the step-up, bloom the rooted target'.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood claimed 'the full package is half a bar at level 3' — a magnitude with no source (defect 6) — and gave no exit cue.
audit.why: The kits carry no damage figures. What they do carry is Frostbite's 4s cooldown, which is the real reason to leave after the bloom rather than stand in the trade.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the sequence plus 'walk before Frostbite recycles at 4s'.

audit.why: The content layer's win condition — kill her before Rebirth, or hold Pop Blossom and E for the egg's re-form — is grounded in Riot's passive text and matches the level chart. It only needed to reach the full layer, where breakdown.carry was a generic deception line.
audit.corrected: breakdown.carry now states the kill-her-twice pattern.

audit.why: Whether Crystallize can block Neeko's Pop Blossom leap, and whether Rebirth has a cooldown long enough to plan a lane around, are both absent from the kit file. Neither was asserted.

notes: Whole full layer was male-templated against a female enemy; 15 fields corrected. Level chart was all 'Skill' in the full layer against a five-row content chart — proposed as one atomic group. dontsFull[1].d told the reader to watch out for 'assassin timers' against Anivia, who has no dash and no stealth; replaced. The Flash Frost -> Frostbite doubling is the single most decisive interaction in this matchup and it appeared nowhere in a form a reader could act on — it is now in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and dontsFull[2].d, with the 1075/650 range gap that makes the pre-6 all-in work in phases[2].why. Fields left templated and ungrounded: breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, loading, tradeBad, report[12].t. No elo tiers written.
